Phenology-driven multisensor unsupervised crop mapping in data-scarce irrigated agriculture: a case of Adea District in Ethiopia
nodes.venue: Water Practice & Technology
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate irrigation planning, water allocation, and agricultural productivity assessment are frequently constrained in data-scare regions where reliable ground-based crop information and spatial coverage data are limited. This study addresses these gaps using a phenology-driven, multisensor unsupervised crop-mapping framework implemented within Google Earth Engine (GEE). The approach integrates monthly normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) profiles from Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1VV backscatter, and digital elevation model–derived terrain slope into unsupervised K-means clustering algorithm. Adea District, Ethiopia, served as a demonstration site to evaluate and interpret the phenological signatures of key irrigated crops. The identified crop types were mapped to estimate spatial coverage and compared with the ground truth observations of irrigated wheat and tomato fields. The approach successfully distinguished irrigated wheat and tomato fields with an overall classification accuracy of 91%, a Kappa coefficient of 0.82, and estimated cultivated areas of 666.93 and 812.35 ha, respectively. Combining phenological profiles with multisensor satellite observations significantly enhance unsupervised classification performance in heterogeneous, smallholder-dominated agricultural landscapes. The cloud-based framework offers a computationally scalable and cost-effective solution for crop mapping, and water productivity monitoring in data-scarce agricultural regions.

nodes.name: Backlighting the Universe with Fast Radio Bursts: An Anthology of Dispersion Measure Cross Correlations with Tracers of Large-scale Structure and Baryonic Matter
nodes.venue: The Astrophysical Journal
nodes.abstract: Abstract Fast radio bursts (FRBs) probe baryons permeating the cosmic web through their dispersion measures (DMs), which encode the integrated electron density along cosmological sight lines. Using 3455 unique FRB sources from CHIME/FRB with ∼15′ localizations, we present an anthology of DM correlations with tracers of large-scale structure and baryonic matter at redshifts z ≲ 1.5. We measured correlations with a vector signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 2.4–5 with 10 probes, including galaxies (2.8), weak gravitational lensing (2.6), cosmic infrared background (4.0), cosmic microwave background (CMB) lensing (3.3), the thermal Sunyaev–Zel’dovich (tSZ) effect (3.8), X-ray emission tracing galaxy clusters (5.0) and superclusters (3.3), soft X-ray background (SXRB, 4.1), and radio continuum emission (3.0). These measurements reveal a consistent picture in which FRB sight lines intersecting overdense environments carry systematically larger DMs. Correlations with hot-gas tracers provide additional leverage on the strength of feedback, as they are strongly weighted toward the dense, bound gas. The measured amplitude of tSZ×DM and SXRB×DM correlations is consistent with theoretical predictions of baryon distribution from a DM– z relation-inferred model with moderate feedback at a ∼0.5 σ level. A weaker feedback scenario is disfavored at ∼3.5 σ by the SXRB×DM correlation under our adopted modeling assumptions. Taken together, these measurements constitute a quantitative multitracer foundation for a new era in which FRBs from next-generation facilities, such as BURSTT, CHORD, the Deep Synoptic Array, and the Square Kilometer Array, in harmony with other probes, will map the baryon content of the full extent of the cosmic web.

nodes.name: Understanding Social Bias in Multimodal Learning Systems: A Taxonomy and Framework
nodes.venue: Machine Learning and Knowledge Extraction
nodes.abstract: The rapid adoption of multimodal learning systems across high-stakes applications has intensified concerns about fairness and social bias, yet existing research remains scattered across modalities, tasks, protected attributes, mitigation strategies, and evaluation methodologies. This survey provides an overview of fairness and social bias in multimodal artificial intelligence. By reviewing 44 papers and 16 datasets, we synthesize the current landscape of fairness research in multimodal systems and identify emerging challenges and research opportunities. Our primary contribution is twofold. First, we introduce a multi-dimensional taxonomy that organizes the literature across nine operational dimensions, providing a unified perspective on multimodal fairness research. Second, we propose an end-to-end operational lifecycle framework that illustrates how biases emerge within shared latent spaces and identifies targeted pre-processing, training-time, and post-training intervention strategies. Overall, this survey discusses key performance-fairness trade-offs and provides a structured roadmap for evaluating and mitigating bias, ultimately supporting the development of more equitable multimodal AI systems.

nodes.name: Three gaps for foundation models to address in satellite remote sensing of inland waters
nodes.abstract: Long-term Earth observation of inland waters depends on continuity between satellite missions, adequate combinations of spectral, spatial and temporal resolution, and representative calibration and validation datasets. Discontinuities and trade-offs in these components constrain the records available for studying inland waters and their change. We examine three gaps affecting inland water remote sensing: a mission gap between comparable 300 m ocean colour observations from MERIS and OLCI during 2012–2016, a coverage gap in spectral, spatial and temporal sampling, and a generalisation gap when retrieval algorithm accuracy declines beyond bio-optical properties and atmospheric conditions represented during development. Foundation models (FMs) could help address these gaps by learning reusable representations from satellite archives before adaptation to a particular retrieval task. We hypothesise that relationships learned across overlapping satellite missions can support reconstruction of what a sensor would have measured during the mission gap, that combining complementary sensors can extend usable observation coverage, and that pretraining on satellite archives, which cover more water bodies and a wider range of bio-optical properties and atmospheric conditions than available field datasets, can improve retrieval algorithm generalisation. Testing these hypotheses requires criteria that define progress. We quantify the three gaps, define a progress criterion for each and assess 100 recent machine learning studies against the criteria. For the mission gap, three studies address continuity across sensor eras, and none recovers a record from a withheld mission period. For the coverage gap, 23 studies combine complementary observations, but only three test them on withheld water bodies or periods. For the generalisation gap, only seven studies withhold whole water bodies or later periods from all model development. Across all three gaps, none of the six studies that use pretraining compares it with the same architecture trained without pretraining on independent water bodies. The assumption common to all three hypotheses, that archive pretraining adds information beyond established methods, therefore remains untested. Applying the criteria to existing generic Earth observation FMs, then to FMs pretrained on inland waters, would determine which gaps pretraining can reduce.

nodes.name: Spatial variations in urban park accessibility and equity under multimodal travel: a case study of Beijing
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Public Health
nodes.abstract: Introduction Equity in urban green space depends not only on whether aggregate park supply is sufficient, but also on how supply aligns with population demand and everyday travel conditions. Methods Taking Beijing as a case study, we represented supply by park area and demand by population distribution. We used the three-step floating catchment area method (3SFCA) to assess accessibility to park green spaces under walking, cycling, and driving. Population-weighted Lorenz curves and Gini coefficients, local bivariate Moran's I, and importance-performance analysis (IPA) were then used to identify inequities and priority areas. Results Accessibility and equity exhibited marked spatial differences. The urban core had the lowest mean accessibility and the strongest overlap between high population demand and low accessibility, making it the primary area for improvement. The urban fringe had higher overall accessibility, but inadequate local green-space service remained pronounced under walking. This pattern reflected a transitional inequity between residential expansion and park provision. The suburb had high mean accessibility but an unequal distribution of walking opportunities, indicating that large-area green-space supply does not necessarily translate into daily access for residents of suburban towns. Park-size classes also performed different functions. District green spaces formed the most stable backbone of area-based accessibility. Regional green spaces relied more on cycling and driving for cross-zone service. Small and micro green spaces and community green spaces were critical for closing local-service gaps in high-density areas. Discussion Beijing should therefore shift from simply increasing green-space area toward coordinated zone-, class-, and mode-specific provision. Local green spaces should be prioritized in the urban core. The urban fringe requires stronger active-travel connections between expanding residential areas and district green spaces. In the suburb, daily access should be improved while large green spaces are protected.

nodes.name: Spatial Variability and Geostatistical Mapping of DTPA-Extractable Cadmium in Surface Soils of Varanasi District, Uttar Pradesh, India
nodes.venue: International Journal of Environment and Climate Change
nodes.abstract: Background: Cadmium (Cd) availability in agricultural soils can show strong local variation, making district-scale averages insufficient for identifying areas of concern. Aims: To describe the spatial variability of DTPA-extractable cadmium (DTPA-Cd) in surface soils of Varanasi district, map it by ordinary kriging and assess the uncertainty of the map. Study Design: Geo-referenced field survey with geostatistical analysis. Place and Duration of Study: Agricultural soils of Varanasi district, Uttar Pradesh, India, sampled between April and May 2026; laboratory analysis was conducted at the Department of Soil Science & Agricultural Chemistry, Institute of Agricultural Sciences, Banaras Hindu University, India. Methodology: Ninety-eight surface soil samples (0 to 15 cm) were collected with GPS coordinates and extracted with DTPA. Data were ln-transformed, and spherical, exponential and Gaussian models were fitted to the experimental semivariogram. Ordinary kriging (OK) and inverse distance weighting (IDW) were compared by leave-one-out cross-validation, and the OK prediction and kriging variance were mapped on a 250 m grid. Results: DTPA-Cd ranged from 0.020 to 6.154 mg kg−1 (mean 0.139, median 0.065 mg kg−1), with a coefficient of variation of 441.9%; 15.3% of samples exceeded 0.1 mg kg−1. The Gaussian model gave the best fit, with a nugget/sill ratio of 42.3% (moderate spatial dependence) and a range parameter of 18.0 km. OK performed slightly better than IDW (RMSE values of 0.616 and 0.619, respectively, on the ln scale), but both explained only 11 to 12% of the variation. Predicted DTPA-Cd ranged from 0.043 to 0.346 mg kg−1, with the highest quartile in the central and eastern parts of the district. Kriging variance was lowest in densely sampled areas and highest in the sparsely sampled centre and along the boundary. Conclusion: Available Cd in the district is generally low but includes isolated high values. The map shows broad regional tendencies, and the extent of the high class depends strongly on a single extreme sample, which needs field verification and denser sampling.

nodes.name: International Journal of Environment and Climate Change
Soil invertebrate biomass estimation from image-derived body area and contour length
nodes.abstract: 1. Soil invertebrate biomass is closely linked to ecosystem processes, yet its routine quantification remains constrained by the effort required to weigh large numbers of small individuals. Length-mass relationships provide an indirect alternative, but body length can be difficult to standardise and extract automatically from images of curved, coiled or contracted organisms. Projected body area may provide a more tractable image-derived predictor, but its performance across diverse soil-faunal taxa and at the community scale remains insufficiently evaluated. 2. Here, we developed a framework using projected body area and contour length to estimate fresh and dry mass from measurements of 1,792 soil invertebrates representing 15 higher-level taxa. We fitted taxon-specific models for six well-represented groups and general models across taxa, and evaluated predictive performance using leave-one-out cross-validation. We then assessed cross-dataset transferability by comparing our data with those of Lemoine et al. (2026) and pooled the two datasets to derive combined models. Finally, we tested whether individual predictions could be scaled to independently measured community biomass. 3. Taxon-specific models generally reduced prediction error relative to general models, with mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) values of 6.9-37.3% for fresh mass and 7.6-30.2% for dry mass. General models retained MAPEs of 27.2% and 22.4%, respectively. Comparisons of our dataset with that of Lemoine et al. (2026) showed no detectable differences in six of eight taxon-by-mass slopes. Although intercepts frequently differed, no overall dataset effect was detected after accounting for taxa. Pooling both datasets broadened model development, while taxon-specific models generally retained lower error than the combined general model. Finally, community-level predictions tracked measured biomass across all model sets (R2 = 0.87-0.99), but absolute error varied among models and faunal groups (MAPE = 9.6-52.5%). 4. Body area and contour length extracted from images therefore provide a practical basis for scaling soil invertebrate biomass estimation from individuals to communities. Integration with automated imaging and segmentation tools such as flatbug, BIODISCOVER and CollembolAI could extend soil invertebrate monitoring at larger scales beyond abundance and taxonomic composition to biomass, while providing scalable inputs for analyses of food webs and general ecosystem ecology.

nodes.name: STAR: Structure-aware representation learning for efficient and robust UAV-based geo-localization
nodes.venue: Communications in Transportation Research
nodes.abstract: Abstract Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based geo-localization supports autonomous navigation in GPS-denied or GPS-degraded environments by matching real-time UAV-view images with geo-referenced satellite imagery. A key challenge is to learn a discriminative retrieval space that remains robust to severe cross-view viewpoint discrepancies and temporal shifts. Although visual appearance provides fine-grained discriminative cues, it is sensitive to illumination, seasonal, and perspective variations. In contrast, geographic structures, such as road layouts and building footprints, offer more stable cues, but explicit structural modeling often increases computational cost. To balance robustness and efficiency, we propose STAR, a lightweight STructure-Aware Representation learning framework. STAR uses structural semantics as training-time geometric guidance for visual retrieval manifold learning. Specifically, a structural stream derives structure-aware representations from paired UAV and satellite images and constructs pairwise structural affinities to describe geographic layout relationships. These affinities regularize the discriminative retrieval space at the manifold level, enabling compact visual descriptors to retain structural awareness for robust cross-view matching. We further introduce UniT-1652, a benchmark for evaluating UAV-based geo-localization under temporal shifts. Extensive experiments on University-1652, SUES-200, and UniT-1652 show that STAR achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple retrieval settings, with improved robustness to temporal and viewpoint variations and fewer parameters than existing methods.

nodes.name: SGKD-FedIDS: Space–Ground Knowledge Distillation for Lightweight Federated Intrusion Detection in Satellite Internet
nodes.venue: Electronics
nodes.abstract: Satellite intrusion detection is challenged by limited on-board resources, heterogeneous traffic, and intermittent satellite–ground links. We propose a space–ground knowledge-distillation-based federated intrusion detection system (SGKD-FedIDS) that transfers attack-discriminative knowledge from a high-capacity ground teacher to a lightweight satellite student. Satellite clients adapt the student to local traffic and upload compressed model updates. The ground federated server aggregates available updates asynchronously and downweights stale ones, avoiding the need to wait for all clients. Experiments across three intrusion detection datasets show that the distilled student achieves an F1-score of 0.9348 on UNSW-NB15, while lightweight federated updating reduces uploaded communication cost by approximately 86.9%. These results support efficient satellite intrusion detection under resource and connectivity constraints.

nodes.name: Preclinical evaluation of a safety-aware multimodal robotic pipeline for human–robot interaction in post-stroke rehabilitation
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Digital Health
nodes.abstract: Introduction Post-stroke rehabilitation increasingly requires technologies capable of supporting intensive, measurable, and adaptable interventions while preserving clinical supervision and patient safety. This study presents a lightweight, safety-aware, and modular multimodal robotic pipeline for embodied human–robot interaction in post-stroke rehabilitation, with a first target application in hemispatial inattention. Methods The system was implemented on the TIAGo mobile manipulator within a ROS 2-based architecture and integrates therapist-mediated supervision, speech-based and graphical interaction, head-orientation monitoring, adaptive auditory recall, robot-mediated and screen-based task delivery, and structured performance logging. Dialogue management is based on a deterministic finite-state machine coupled with a rule-based Natural Language Understanding pipeline, enabling predictable interaction handling, explicit fallback behavior, and therapist escalation for safety-relevant events. A preliminary preclinical evaluation was conducted in 16 healthy participants, with a repeated acquisition after 1 month. The study assessed operational feasibility, multimodal interaction robustness, head-orientation monitoring stability, task execution, ASR-related interaction events, usability, acceptance, and 1-month reproducibility of workflow execution. Results All participants completed both acquisitions without adverse events or safety-relevant events requiring interruption of the experimental workflow. End-effector recognition accuracy remained high, attention-recall events were infrequent, screen-based visual tasks were successfully administered and logged, and usability and acceptance outcomes were favorable, with low anxiety toward the robotic platform. Discussion These findings support the feasibility of using a therapist-supervised robotic platform as an integrated tool for structured interaction, head-orientation monitoring, rehabilitation-oriented task delivery, and quantitative logging. The study presents a preclinical evaluation of system architecture, safety-aware interaction design, and workflow robustness. Future work is organized in two stages: a dedicated acceptance and robustness protocol in healthy controls to formally test interaction acceptance, speech-recognition robustness, and safety-relevant failure handling, followed by a true rehabilitation protocol in post-stroke patients with hemispatial inattention, including therapist-supervised exercise adaptation.

nodes.name: Photon-Counting Computed Tomography Enables Image-Guided Navigation of the Paranasal Sinuses at Ultra-Low Radiation Dose: An Initial Cadaveric Study
nodes.venue: Diagnostics
nodes.abstract: Background/Objectives: Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) enables substantial radiation dose reduction while preserving high spatial resolution. Its potential for image-guided navigation in endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS), particularly at ultra-low dose levels, remains insufficiently explored. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of PCCT for four different surgical navigation systems at progressively reduced radiation doses. Methods: PCCT datasets of the paranasal sinuses were acquired from two cadaveric specimens using a standard protocol followed by stepwise dose reductions down to 5% of the reference dose. The datasets were used for image-guided navigation with four systems (one optical, three electromagnetic). Registration success, navigation accuracy, and user satisfaction (visual analog scale) were assessed at 100% and 5% dose levels using linear mixed-effects models. Results: Registration was successful for all navigation systems at every dose level. Mean navigation accuracy remained stable despite dose reduction (2.22 ± 1.16 mm at 100% vs. 1.93 ± 1.05 mm at 5% radiation dose; p = 0.364). User satisfaction regarding navigation was consistently high (mean 8.8 ± 0.75) and showed no significant differences between dose levels. Conclusions: PCCT enabled image-guided navigation even at ultra-low radiation doses down to 5% of standard exposure, without compromising navigation accuracy in this initial study. These findings highlight the potential of PCCT to substantially reduce radiation burden while maintaining clinical performance. Further in-human studies are needed.

nodes.name: On-fault and remote observations of exceptionally long, supershear rupture in the 2025 M 7.7 Mandalay earthquake
nodes.venue: Science Advances
nodes.abstract: Straight faults are considered prone to large supershear ruptures and seismic gaps to likely host future earthquakes. Both predictions may have been fulfilled in the magnitude ( M ) 7.7 Mandalay earthquake of 28 March 2025 on the Sagaing Fault. Exceptional video footage of the fault rupture, high-rate Global Navigation Satellite System, and seismological and remote sensing data reveal a supershear slip pulse that formed early and ruptured a well-identified seismic gap but propagated well beyond it, resulting in an exceptional rupture length of 510 kilometers. By contrast, the slip pulse observed in the video footage has subshear characteristics. These observations can be reconciled by a preferred conceptual interpretation invoking depth-dependent weakening properties, stress heterogeneity, and possible dynamic triggering. These properties allow for energetic ruptures that stay confined to the depth range locked in the interseismic period but are not confined to seismic gaps along strike.

nodes.name: Multi-spectral semantic segmentation and localization framework for ecosystem monitoring using Visible–SWIR satellite imagery
nodes.venue: Optics and Photonics for Information Processing XX
nodes.abstract: This study proposes a Visible–SWIR multispectral semantic segmentation and geospatial localization framework for ecosystem monitoring. The method fuses Visible, SWIR1, SWIR2, NDVI, NBR, NBR2, NDMI, and brightness temperature features to enhance the identification of vegetation, moisture, burned surfaces, and thermal anomalies. The segmentation outputs are converted into object-level descriptors—class, area, centroid, distance, and orientation—and paired with satellite metadata and coordinate constraints to enable localization. In the Kangaroo Island wildfire case study, the proposed method correctly detected 5,295 fire pixels, achieving 90.51% precision, 80.32% recall, an F1 score of 85.11%, and an IoU of 74.09%. Results show that multispectral fusion improves fire-core recognition and boundary continuity while mitigating single-band misclassifications caused by smoke, clouds, and surface heterogeneity. The proposed framework can be further applied to land-cover evaluation, vegetation monitoring, disaster assessment, and time-series ecological change detection.

nodes.name: Optics and Photonics for Information Processing XX
Monitoring of Sows’ Standing Reflex During Estrus Based on Machine Vision
nodes.venue: Agriculture
nodes.abstract: Monitoring estrus in sows is crucial for enhancing the efficiency of production management in pig farms. Standing reflex, as a clear sign of estrus and the optimal timing indicator for artificial insemination, has lacked an efficient and reliable method for monitoring. This study developed an approach based on machine vision for the automated detection of standing reflex in multiple sows within stalls. Specifically, a detection strategy was proposed based on the analysis of movement patterns by first calculating the Intersection over Union (IoU) sequence for each sow, followed by classification of standing reflex versus non-standing reflex sequences using a Convolutional–BiLSTM–Attention (CBA) network. Additionally, the lying targets were excluded from sequential classification while employing the improved YOLOv8 for segmentation. A total of 1484 images were captured for instance segmentation, and 445 IoU sequences were extracted from videos for temporal classification. Experimental results showed that misclassification rate of the improved YOLOv8 was 3% in distinguishing between lying and standing postures, indicating its efficiency in identifying these two states. Moreover, the mean average precision (mAP) of segmentation reached 98.2%, with a detection latency of 7.8 ms per image, demonstrating the model’s efficient capability in extracting target contours. The CBA model achieved an accuracy of 96.6 ± 2.7%. The proposed method enabled accurate monitoring of standing reflex in sows, facilitating more precise control over breeding times.

nodes.name: Measuring rock strain with distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) and cemented patch cables
nodes.venue: Geophysical Journal International
nodes.abstract: Summary A rigid connection between the optical fiber and the rock allows to properly measure ‘rock strain’ with Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS). We demonstrate this by running four interrogator units (IU) on a testbed with single-fiber patch cables being cemented into a groove in the concrete floor of Black Forest Observatory (BFO). The recorded signals are compared with the recordings of a calibrated Invar wire strain meter array that has been continuously in operation for the last decades at a distance of about 350 m to the testbed. In this way we compare the ‘fiber strain’ against ‘rock strain’ at frequencies below 0.2 Hz. We investigate this on the background of a previous study with DAS cables unreeled on the floor and loaded down by sand and sandbags, where we found a significant loss of strain amplitude between rock and fiber. Waveform similarity for strong earthquake signals is high with typical values of the normalized correlation coefficient greater than 0.95. The strain amplitude measured by all four IUs is very consistent and by about 10 per cent larger than the strain measured by the strainmeters. We attribute this minor discrepancy to spatially varying strain-strain coupling caused by the local topography. At frequencies up to 14 Hz we make an intercomparison of IUs, showing no significant variation with frequency. The scatter of strain amplitude in between channels which are spatially near to each other in the same fiber route is about ±10 per cent in most cases. The variation of median values in between different IUs and earthquakes is less than 5 per cent. By subtracting the common mode noise, which is coherent along the fiber route, we lower the background signal level to an rms-amplitude of 100 pstrain at 0.1 Hz and 5 pstrain at 1 Hz in a bandwidth of 1/6 decade for the best cases. This allows the detection of the marine microseisms during times of moderate amplitude level.

nodes.name: Marine litter in the Mediterranean: observation-based Lagrangian particle tracking
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Marine Science
nodes.abstract: Introduction The Mediterranean is a major hotspot for floating marine macro-litter (FMML) accumulation, yet spatially explicit, observation-grounded predictions of its transport and coastal deposition remain scarce. We present a data-driven stochastic Lagrangian framework that uses monthly gridded FMML observations from systematic shipboard surveys as simulation initial conditions complementing existing source-based modelling approaches. Methods Observations were collected from August 2023 to December 2024 within the LIFE Conceptu Maris Project using ferries as monitoring platforms under a standardised protocol. A total of 158 surveys detected 4,801 FMML items across approximately 6,200 km² of surveyed sea surface, of which more than 62% were artificial polymers. Observed monthly FMML item counts at 5 × 5 km resolution initialised ensemble Lagrangian simulations (18 members per target month; 17.2–32.5 million virtual particles per seeding window, 5,000 particles per observed item) using Parcels, forced by Copernicus Marine Service Mediterranean reanalysis currents and ERA5 wind fields with a 1% windage coefficient and a 2D random-walk turbulent diffusion scheme. Monthly frequency-of-occurrence maps were computed at the sea surface and on coastlines. Results The Southern Tyrrhenian and Northern Ligurian seas, including the Pelagos Sanctuary, exhibited in 2024 near-persistent high sea surface FMML occurrence, peaking in late summer–autumn and reaching a seasonal minimum in winter–early spring. The Balearic Sea showed elevated occurrence from late spring through summer (May–September), declining through autumn. The Adriatic displayed intense sub-basin-scale spreading from January to June and again in December, with summer leakage into the Northern Ionian Sea. Coastal deposition frequencies were highest on Corsica, western Sardinia and northern Tunisia, then the south-eastern Tyrrhenian and Ligurian–Tuscan margins, with Valencia–Barcelona largely confined to summer. Integration with loggerhead turtle nesting records illustrates how coastal frequency-of-occurrence maps can support conservation applications. Discussion A web-based Particle Analysis Dashboard translates these outputs into an interactive tool with Marine Protected and Conserved Area overlays for scientists and decision-makers. The framework provides a scalable, observation-anchored foundation for MSFD Descriptor 10 monitoring, transferable to other semi-enclosed sea basins. Priority future work includes complementary validation against independent beach-litter monitoring data, integration of land-based source inventories, and linkage with species distribution models.

nodes.name: Magnetic Detection of Deeply Buried Impact Craters on Earth
nodes.abstract: Most traces of past impacts with cosmic bodies that occurred on Earth during Time have been erased by geological processes, such as subduction and erosion, have been hidden by sedimentation and volcanism, or have been covered by seawater; the Moon, the Earth’s natural satellite, may be considered our best scientific laboratory for impact cratering processes. The number of accepted and recorded impact craters on Earth suddenly increased when observations have been taken from the above the Earth from airplanes, satellites and drones. The number of accepted and recorded old impacts on Earth recently started to increase when scientists turned toward the deeply located buried craters, using Geophysics. The available recorded impacts have been completed with re-cently published large diameter of buried impact structures: Precaspian Depression, situated in Kazakhstan and Russia (ca 700 km), Alexandria Depression, situated in Romania and Bulgaria (ca 175 km) and Transylvanian Depression, situated in Romania (ca 300 km). The recorded impacts suggest that a correlation with life extinction events can be made in Devonian (Fras-nian-Famennian) and at the Cretaceous-Tertiary boundary, Chicxulub event being known world-wide. It is likely that large diameter impactors on Earth might represent a necessary condi-tion for relating impacts with cosmic bodies to high extinction events. Large diameter asteroids, interpreted to have created the Precaspian and Alexandria depressions during the Permian may be well correlated with the Maokouan (50% life extinction) and Changhsingian (78% life extinction). On the three discussed study cases, the Bouguer gravity anomaly was the main geophysical in-formation for detecting a buried impact structure; besides the traditional gravity low, high gravity anomalies associated with the uplifted Crater rim and Central peak are being interpreted. The magnetic anomalies of the Precaspian region illustrate a circular sector with high magnetic anom-alies, interpreted as effects of the uplifted magnetic basement along the Crater rim and partly, effect of the magnetic “step effect” above abruptly ended magnetic geological formations. The magnetic anomalies over the Alexandria Depression proved to be weak and less associated to the impact structure; the crater uplifted sectors have been probably eroded and its infrastructure masked by the effect of thick lava flows, embedded in the depression sedimentary infill. The magnetic data of the Transylvanian Depression contradicts the usual way magnetic anomalies are interpreted above impact structures, a large and intense high magnetic anomaly being measured, instead of a large magnetic low. This anomaly, aided by a magnetic 2D modeling, was interpreted as effect of a huge magmatic structure, a batholith, intruded suite of geological processes determined by the asteroid impact.

nodes.name: Leakage-aware pre-match prediction of professional volleyball outcomes: temporal validation of machine-learning models against an Elo baseline
nodes.abstract: Abstract Background Volleyball performance studies often identify technical statistics that distinguish winners after matches are completed, but such variables are not necessarily valid predictors before a match. This study evaluated professional volleyball outcome forecasting under an explicit prediction-time information boundary, with particular attention to data leakage, temporal validation, probability calibration, and comparison with a transparent team-strength baseline. Methods A public Polish PlusLiga dataset contained 2,639 match records. A targeted schema audit identified an historical column-mapping problem in all 2,011 records from 2008/09-2018/19 under the current headers; the source file contains no 2019/20 rows. The primary analysis therefore used 628 matches from the source-labelled 2020/21-2022/23 periods. Seventeen predictors were constructed sequentially before each match: an Elo rating differential, 14 differences based on each team's previous up-to-five matches, a history-availability differential, and a rest-days differential. Matches from 2020/21-2021/22 formed the development cohort (n = 424), with five expanding time-series folds for hyperparameter selection. The 2022/23 observations in the source dataset were withheld from model fitting and tuning (n = 204). Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, a multilayer perceptron, and XGBoost were compared with Elo and prevalence baselines. Results Logistic Regression had the highest observed ROC-AUC on the held-out cohort (0.7941; 95% outcome-stratified bootstrap CI 0.7296–0.8528), with accuracy 0.7206, F1 0.7421, Brier score 0.1880, and log loss 0.5614. Random Forest produced a similar AUC (0.7811) and identical accuracy (0.7206). The Elo baseline was competitive (AUC 0.7629; accuracy 0.7059). The paired AUC difference between Logistic Regression and Elo was 0.0312 (95% CI 0.0047–0.0584), whereas the difference between Logistic Regression and Random Forest was 0.0130 (95% CI -0.0138 to 0.0403). Permutation importance for Logistic Regression was dominated by the pre-match Elo differential; individual recent-form variables made substantially smaller contributions. Conclusions Under leakage-aware and time-ordered evaluation, professional volleyball match outcomes were moderately predictable rather than near-perfectly classifiable. A simple Elo strength rating captured much of the available signal, and more complex learners did not show a large, consistent advantage. The findings support cautious pre-match decision support, not live in-game deployment, causal coaching prescriptions, or cross-league generalization. Independent external validation with harmonized historical predictors remains necessary.

nodes.name: Instruction-Following LLM Agent for Simulating Human Memory Retrieval Process in Household Tasks
nodes.venue: Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting
nodes.abstract: Human decision-making in dynamic household environments depends on memory retrieval processes that shape action selection and timing. This paper presents an instruction-following LLM agent as an executable human performance model for simulating memory retrieval behavior in household tasks. The proposed framework integrates memory encoding and decision-making modules with a modified ACT-R base-level activation equation that incorporates environmental entropy and observation duration. The framework was evaluated using human behavioral data from an AI2-THOR-based household task study. When predicting human search times, the modified equation produced lower prediction errors than the conventional ACT-R baseline, reducing MAE, RMSE, and MAPE by 11.08%, 5.37%, and 16.00%, respectively. These findings provide preliminary evidence that incorporating context-sensitive retrieval factors may support closer alignment with human search-time behavior in executable LLM-based human performance models.

nodes.name: Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting
Enriched-nonexpansive Plug-and-Play image restoration
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Applied Mathematics and Statistics
nodes.abstract: Plug-and-Play methods solve imaging inverse problems by inserting a learned denoiser into a proximal splitting algorithm. Their convergence theory presently requires the denoiser, or its residual, to be nonexpansive or firmly nonexpansive, a constraint that curbs the network and, in turn, the reconstruction quality. We prove that this requirement can be weakened to enriched nonexpansivity, a strictly larger operator class in which the map is nonexpansive only after averaging. Using the displacement and transfer–return calculus for nonexpansive-type operators, we show that when the composite Plug-and-Play operator is enriched nonexpansive an inertial Mann or Ishikawa iteration converges to a fixed point of the operator, that is, to a Plug-and-Play solution, and we identify the inertial correction as the exact quantity that reduces the enriched iteration to a classical iteration of the nonexpansive generator. Around this reduction we build a certification theory. The operator is b -enriched exactly when the displacement I− T is infinitesimally cocoercive with modulus 1/(2( b +1)), so that the smallest admissible constant is one less than the supremum of a Rayleigh-type quotient of that displacement. The characterization is attained on non-scalar operators, is computable by automatic differentiation, and remains bounded in the near-identity regime where the field-of-values bound degenerates. A perturbation estimate converts spectral measurements on a finite sample into a bound over a segment or a covered set, which is what the Fejér argument needs and what a program can carry out. We add a training objective that promotes the certified inequality, a safeguarded step-size controller with a closed-form greedy rule and an amortized policy trained by unrolled differentiation, sublinear and linear rates, stability under inexact denoiser evaluation, and a splitting-agnostic extension covering Plug-and-Play ADMM. Two experiments support the theory. On a linear surrogate, for which every constant is available in closed form, the certificates are confirmed and the exact characterization widens the admissible step-size window by about 31% over the field-of-values bound. On Gaussian deblurring, motion deblurring and single-image super-resolution with trained denoisers, the certified constant is measured for each composite operator. On the deblurring task a trained composite with Lipschitz constant 2.08, admitted by no nonexpansive condition, is certified with constant 0.60, where the characterization is more than fifteen times tighter than the field-of-values bound; it restores within four hundredths of a decibel of a nonexpansive composite of identical architecture, so the larger class is reached at no measured cost in quality. The greedy relaxation halves the iteration count of the constant-step scheme. The acceleration is measured among safeguarded schemes; unrelaxed Picard, which carries no guarantee here, remains faster on the linear instance.

nodes.name: Frontiers in Applied Mathematics and Statistics
Emotional Expression, Treatment Discussions, and Peer Support in Online Fibromyalgia Communities: Large-Scale Natural Language Processing Analysis
nodes.abstract: Abstract Purpose: Fibromyalgia is a long-term medical condition associated with widespread pain, fatigue, diagnostic uncertainty, and persistent unmet patient needs, including feeling misunderstood, inadequately supported, and uncertain about treatment. Individuals often turn to online communities for information, validation, and peer support, generating digital health data that can provide insights into lived experience beyond traditional clinical settings. Methods: A total of 66,611 publicly available posts published between 2013 and 2025 from an online fibromyalgia community were analysed. Three topic-modelling approaches (LDA, NMF and BERTopic) were comparatively evaluated and integrated with a custom 12-category, domain-specific emotion and communication taxonomy developed specifically for fibromyalgia and chronic-illness discourse. LLM-based classification was used to characterise thematic, emotional and peer-support patterns at scale. Medication discourse was additionally analysed for emotional associations and geographic variation. Results: Patient discussions linked symptom burden with emotional distress and treatment experiences. Frustration, anxiety, uncertainty, and support-seeking frequently accompanied discussions of pain, healthcare experiences, and medication use. Highly active members contributed disproportionately to peer support. Ninety-six distinct medications and supplements were identified, with low-dose naltrexone the most frequently discussed treatment (3,977 mentions). Medication discussions showed distinct emotional patterns, with conventional treatments frequently associated with distress and some complementary or experimental therapies associated with hope, resilience and peer support. Conclusions: Large-scale computational analysis of patient-generated digital health data identified patterns of fibromyalgia experience consistent with those previously observed through manual qualitative research, while enabling their systematic examination across substantially larger volumes of patient discourse. This scalable approach provides insight into patient priorities, treatment perceptions, and unmet support needs that may be less visible during conventional clinical encounters, with relevance to patient-centred digital health services and clinician–patient communication.

nodes.name: Electromagnetic Localization 6-DoF Pose Estimation with TGNet-Guided Initial Value Refinement
nodes.venue: Mathematics
nodes.abstract: High-precision electromagnetic localization shows great promise for applications in medical treatment, embodied intelligence, entertainment, and gaming. However, six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) coil pose estimation is essentially a highly nonlinear inverse problem. Numerical iterative solvers, such as the Levenberg–Marquardt (LM) algorithm, are sensitive to poor initial guesses and prone to getting trapped in local optima. This limitation has become a major bottleneck for improving the accuracy and robustness of electromagnetic localization systems. To address this problem, we propose a network termed TGNet (Transmitter Geometry-guided Network) that provides reliable initial guesses for the iterative solver. The network mainly consists of three parts: (i) a dual-branch module that encodes the spatial distribution of the transmitting coil as physical priors, thereby narrowing the ambiguous solution space and effectively mitigating pose ambiguity arising from multiple local extrema; (ii) a decoupled regression head that estimates the coil’s 6-DoF position and orientation independently, reducing cross-coupling complexity; and (iii) a numerical simulation-based data generation strategy that produces large-scale datasets of magnetic field measurements paired with ground-truth 6-DoF poses for fully supervised training, circumventing the difficulty of collecting real-world labeled data. Using TGNet predictions as initial guesses for the LM algorithm, we achieved average position and orientation errors of 1.5 mm and 0.6°, respectively, in real localization experiments. In contrast, using random data as initial guesses for the LM algorithm, the average position and orientation errors were 31.1 mm and 7.9°, confirming that the proposed initialization improves accuracy. First, TGNet reliably avoids local minima, as the LM algorithm converges at all test points in the localization space. Second, TGNet reduces the iteration counts of the LM algorithm, decreasing them from 39 to 14. Overall, TGNet provides a robust and efficient solution for high-performance electromagnetic localization.

nodes.name: Deep Learning-Based Detection and Localization of Forged Caste Certificates Using Convolutional Neural Networks and Gradient-Weighted Class Activation Mapping
nodes.venue: International Journal for Research In Science & Advanced Technologies
nodes.abstract: Government-issued caste certificates serve as a gateway to constitutional benefits reserved for socially and economically disadvantaged communities in India. Growing misuse of image manipulation tools to fabricate such documents has created an urgent need for reliable automated verification mechanisms. This study introduces a deep-learning solution, referred to as LOCATE, that performs both classification and spatial fault-finding on suspect certificates. A four-layer Convolutional Neural Network trained on a purpose-built collection of 1,000 Karnataka state certificates (500 genuine, 500 manipulated) first separates authentic documents from tampered ones. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping then pinpoints the exact region within a flagged document that triggered the forgery verdict, giving human reviewers a clear visual basis for their decisions. At operating threshold τ = 0.7, the system attains 98% overall accuracy, 100% precision, 96% recall, and an F1-score of 0.98, while preserving 100% specificity. These results surpass all comparable prior approaches and demonstrate that the framework is ready for real-world administrative deployment.

nodes.name: Subramani, Muralidhara B L, Suresh R C
International Journal for Research In Science & Advanced Technologies
Content Deviation Recognition and Recommendation Model for Sports and Health Information: Based on Improved Text Rank Algorithm and Deep Fusion Transformer Architecture
nodes.abstract: Abstract Misleading and unsubstantiated information is widely circulated in the field of sports and health. Digital platforms amplify such content through recommendation systems, potentially influencing users’ health behaviors. This study first constructed a training corpus for identifying content bias and recommending sports health information, based on the Text REtrieval Conference (TREC) Health Misinformation Track dataset. Next, the original TextRank framework was enhanced by incorporating context-aware semantic vectors generated via Sentence Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (SBERT). These vectors formed a semantic-aware graph structure, with edge weights defined by semantic similarity. This approach improved the model’s ability to capture implicit bias information. A source credibility modeling mechanism was also introduced. It calculated a “source confidence score” based on the publishing organization or platform. This score was incorporated as a model input or ranking feature to reduce the overexposure of low-credibility content. Additionally, content with high bias and low source weight could be assigned to a “restricted dissemination candidate set”, supporting subsequent verification against authoritative databases. Finally, a multi-level Transformer architecture combining Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and Longformer was constructed. BERT extracted local semantic features during encoding, while the output stage used a multi-task learning mechanism to perform bias classification and relevance prediction. This enabled a joint recommendation system based on content credibility and user interest relevance. Experimental results showed that, in the bias identification subtask, the proposed model achieved an overall F1-score of 92.7% on the TREC dataset. This outperformed Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach (RoBERTa)-base (89.1%), Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining for Language Understanding (XLNet)-large (87.6%), and the medical-domain pre-trained model ERNIE-Health (90.3%). In the recommendation task, a ranking mechanism based on content credibility and relevance prediction led to relative improvements of 8.3% in Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at rank 10 (nDCG@10) and 6.5% in Mean Average Precision (MAP). For “exercise methods” queries, the model achieved an F1-score of 94.2% in bias identification. For “supplements and nutritional interventions” queries, nDCG@10 increased by 9.1%, significantly outperforming baseline models. Incorporating the source credibility feature further improved the accuracy of high-bias, low-weight document identification by 3.4% and substantially reduced the ranking weight of such content in recommendation results. Overall, the proposed model enhanced the accuracy of biased information detection and integrated source credibility modeling and ranking control mechanisms to regulate content exposure.

nodes.name: Chem-AI: Reframing AI-Assisted Research Through Structured, Retrieval-Based Scientific Literature Analysis
nodes.venue: UC Riverside Undergraduate Research Journal
nodes.abstract: The growing volume of scientific literature presents a significant challenge for researchers to identify relevant methods, compare findings, and build upon existing work. Although advances in artificial intelligence have led to new tools for literature analysis, many of these tools rely on generative models whose outputs are not always grounded in verifiable sources. This raises concerns about reliability and reproducibility in scientific research. In this study, we explore whether a retrieval-based system can provide more transparent and trustworthy support throughout the research process. We present Chem-AI, an interactive tool that structures the research process into clear steps, including query interpretation, literature retrieval, experiment classification, and method mapping. Unlike conventional AI systems that generate answers without clear justification, Chem-AI links each output directly to published research, allowing users to trace and verify the information. The system was evaluated using a diverse set of chemistry research queries spanning reaction mechanisms and analytical techniques. Compared to standard generative models, Chem-AI retrieved more relevant sources (with roughly 95% of responses rated as fully relevant), produced responses grounded in established methods, and reduced unsupported or unverifiable claims. These results suggest that a retrieval-based approach improves both the reliability and clarity of AI-assisted research. By aligning with the structure of real research workflows, Chem-AI provides a more transparent and user-centered way to navigate scientific literature. This approach is especially useful for undergraduate researchers, supporting more accurate, reproducible, and methodologically grounded work.

nodes.name: Bloom Filter Data Summarization: A High-Throughput Spatial Representation Approach for Network Traffic Classification
nodes.abstract: Abstract Network traffic monitoring requires high-throughput processing of massive, heterogeneous data streams, making lightweight data summarization essential for real-time threat analysis. This paper proposes a resource-efficient representation technique utilizing a deterministic Bloom Filter architecture to aggregate network flows into two-dimensional sliding window bitmaps. By transforming variable-length traffic data into fixed-size spatial representations, we enable the direct application of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for rapid threat classification without the overhead of complex, per-packet feature engineering. The main contributions are three-fold: (i) a low-latency, Bloom-filter-based spatial encoding technique for network-flow sliding windows; (ii) the deployment of CNNs for robust threat detection utilizing this compact bitmap representation; and (iii) an optimized, GPU-accelerated pipeline designed for scalable environments. Evaluated on a real-world broadband dataset from a Brazilian access provider, our approach demonstrates high classification precision (> 0.90) and recall (≈ 0.80) for detecting high-risk traffic windows while maintaining minimal computational overhead.

nodes.name: Absolute localisation in global navigation satellite system–denied navigation: Comparative robustness of adventitious and engineered landmark anchoring
nodes.venue: The Journal of Defense Modeling and Simulation: Applications, Methodology, Technology
nodes.abstract: Reliable absolute localisation over kilometre-scale trajectories in global navigation satellite system-denied environments remains a fundamental challenge for small autonomous aerial vehicles. Visual–inertial odometry and simultaneous localisation and mapping provide accurate short-term motion estimates but accumulate drift, requiring periodic absolute correction from external references. Two principal strategies exist: alignment to adventitious scene landmarks derived from prior mapping, and detection of deployed engineered fiducial markers. This article develops a neutral probabilistic framework to compare these approaches. We introduce Landmark Integrity as a unified descriptor of reference persistence, visibility, and identification reliability, and show that both adventitious landmark anchoring and engineered landmark anchoring reduce to robust subset selection within a field of potentially unreliable markers. A closed-form expression is derived for terminal localisation success probability as a function of usable landmark density, integrity, and required accuracy. Using literature-informed modelling priors across representative terrains and illumination conditions, we identify regimes where adventitious landmark anchoring suffices, but also identify regimes fundamentally limited by scene structure. Metre-scale terminal accuracy in low-texture or degraded-visibility environments is unlikely to be achievable by adventitious landmark anchoring alone, whereas engineered landmark anchoring maintains high reliability within a confined terminal region. These results motivate hybrid architectures combining adventitious landmark anchoring acquisition with engineered landmark anchoring or terminal seekers for precision.
