ACESSIBILIDADE CULTURAL E CONSTRUÇÃO DA IDENTIDADE VISUAL DO PROJETO SINALART
nodes.venue: Entre Áreas e Saberes: Abordagens Multidisciplinares na Pesquisa Científica
nodes.abstract: Este estudo objetiva analisar o processo de construção da identidade visual do projeto de extensão SinalArt, vinculado à Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ). Justifica-se o estudo porque a acessibilidade cultural contemporânea exige que a Língua Brasileira de Sinais (Libras) transcenda a mera função de instrumento adaptador, constituindo-se como língua legítima de criação, expressão e fruição estética. Fundamenta-se o trabalho nos preceitos teóricos da acessibilidade cultural e dos direitos das pessoas com deficiência (BRASIL, 2008; 2015; DORNELES et al., 2018), nos conceitos de branding e gestão de marcas aplicados à comunicação institucional (KUEHLWEIN; SCHAEFER, 2021; BEDENDO, s/d), bem como na perspectiva semiótica e multimodal da linguagem (ECO,2014; KRESS, 2010). Quanto à metodologia, a pesquisa caracteriza-se como qualitativa, de natureza bibliográfica e documental, empregando como corpus um vídeo institucional do projeto para examinar como a tipografia, a paleta cromática, os elementos gráfico-simbólicos e a identidade linguística se articulam na consolidação da marca. Como resultados preliminares, aponta-se que a nova identidade visual sintetiza com eficácia a união entre a manualidade da Libras e o universo das artes visuais, garantindo que a comunicação do projeto se mantenha clara, inclusiva e coerente com seus propósitos institucionais. Palavras-chaves: Acessibilidade Cultural. Libras. Branding. INTRODUÇÃO Este estudo objetiva analisar o processo de construção da identidade visual do projeto de extensão SinalArt, vinculado à Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ), desenvolvido pelo designer Monique Mairins, considerando que a constituição de uma marca institucional, especialmente quando vinculada a uma iniciativa de caráter extensionista, não se restringe à elaboração de elementos gráficos, mas participa da produção de sentidos, da representação de identidades e da legitimação de determinadas práticas sociais e culturais. Nesse contexto, o SinalArt assume relevância social, cultural e política ao promover a Língua Brasileira de Sinais (Libras) como língua de criação, expressão e fruição artística, contribuindo para que pessoas surdas ocupem espaços de produção, circulação e reconhecimento cultural, ao mesmo tempo em que amplia, no âmbito da universidade pública, as possibilidades de participação e acessibilidade nos diferentes campos das artes. A relevância deste estudo fundamenta-se na compreensão de que a acessibilidade cultural contemporânea, para além da eliminação de barreiras comunicacionais e físicas, pressupõe a garantia de condições para que diferentes sujeitos possam produzir, acessar, interpretar e vivenciar manifestações culturais em suas próprias línguas e modos de expressão. Desse modo, o SinalArt, ao articular Libras, artes e extensão universitária, constitui-se como espaço de valorização da diversidade linguística e cultural, de enfrentamento de barreiras historicamente impostas à participação de pessoas surdas e de fortalecimento do direito à cultura e à comunicação. Além de sua dimensão social e cultural, a atuação do projeto apresenta uma dimensão política, na medida em que a presença da Libras nos espaços universitários e artísticos contribui para tensionar concepções segundo as quais as línguas de sinais ocupariam posição secundária ou exerceriam exclusivamente funções de acessibilidade. Ao promover a circulação da Libras em diferentes linguagens artísticas e ao conferir visibilidade às produções realizadas nessa língua, o SinalArt participa de um movimento de reconhecimento linguístico e cultural que se relaciona diretamente às políticas de inclusão, acessibilidade e direitos das pessoas com deficiência. Assim, a construção de sua identidade visual também pode ser compreendida como uma prática comunicacional que materializa valores institucionais e sociais, uma vez que os signos empregados na marca não apenas identificam o projeto, mas também comunicam seus princípios, seus públicos e seu posicionamento diante da diversidade linguística e cultural. A investigação fundamenta-se, portanto, nos preceitos teóricos da acessibilidade cultural e dos direitos das pessoas com deficiência (BRASIL, 2008; 2015; DORNELES et al., 2018), nos conceitos de branding e gestão de marcas aplicados à comunicação institucional (KUEHLWEIN; SCHAEFER, 2021; BEDENDO, s/d), bem como na perspectiva semiótica e multimodal da linguagem (ECO, 2014; KRESS, 2010). Parte-se do pressuposto de que, embora os elementos visuais sejam frequentemente associados a uma dimensão predominantemente estética, sua organização, quando orientada por uma estratégia de comunicação, contribui para a construção de significados e para a consolidação de uma identidade institucional, especialmente quando essa identidade está vinculada a questões linguísticas, culturais e sociais. Quanto à metodologia, a pesquisa caracteriza-se como qualitativa, de natureza bibliográfica e documental, empregando como corpus um vídeo institucional do projeto, por meio do qual são examinados os modos como a tipografia, a paleta cromática, os elementos gráfico-simbólicos e a identidade linguística se articulam na consolidação da marca. Busca-se, desse modo, compreender de que maneira os diferentes recursos semióticos e multimodais empregados na identidade visual contribuem para comunicar os valores e os propósitos do SinalArt, considerando-se que a construção de uma marca institucional ocorre mediante a articulação entre aspectos visuais, linguísticos, culturais e discursivos. Como resultados preliminares, aponta-se que a nova identidade visual sintetiza a relação entre a manualidade e a visualidade próprias da Libras e o universo das artes visuais, ao mesmo tempo em que estabelece uma comunicação coerente com os princípios de acessibilidade, diversidade e valorização da cultura surda que orientam o projeto. Observa-se, ainda, que a articulação entre os diferentes elementos visuais contribui para conferir unidade à comunicação institucional, favorecendo o reconhecimento da marca e ampliando sua capacidade de representar um projeto que, ao inserir a Libras no campo das práticas artísticas e acadêmicas, produz efeitos que ultrapassam a dimensão comunicacional e alcançam as esferas social, cultural e política. O presente estudo encontra-se estruturado em quatro seções, que orientam o percurso analítico desenvolvido. Na primeira seção, aborda-se o conceito de acessibilidade cultural, demonstrando-se como o projeto SinalArt articula a Libras e as práticas artísticas no contexto da universidade pública e como essa articulação contribui para a ampliação da participação cultural de pessoas surdas. Na segunda seção, apresenta-se a fundamentação teórica sobre branding, evidenciando-se que a gestão estratégica de marcas, embora envolva aspectos visuais, ultrapassa a dimensão estética ao participar da construção de identidades, valores e posicionamentos institucionais. Na terceira seção, detalha-se o percurso metodológico, explicando-se de que maneira a abordagem qualitativa, a pesquisa bibliográfica e documental e a perspectiva multimodal subsidiam a análise do objeto investigado. Por fim, na quarta seção, desenvolve-se a análise dos resultados obtidos, verificando-se como os elementos visuais e linguísticos da nova identidade visual traduzem a essência e os valores do SinalArt e contribuem para a construção de uma marca que articula comunicação, acessibilidade, arte, identidade linguística e reconhecimento cultural.

nodes.name: Entre Áreas e Saberes: Abordagens Multidisciplinares na Pesquisa Científica
A deep learning-driven image processing pipeline for differential classification of atypical Parkinsonian disorders
nodes.venue: Emerging Topics in Artificial Intelligence (ETAI) 2026
nodes.abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis of atypical Parkinsonian disorders (APD), including progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and multiple system atrophy (MSA), remains a major clinical challenge due to overlapping symptoms with Parkinson’s disease (PD), particularly in early disease stages. Three dimensional (3D) segmentation of brain structures from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has the potential to provide supportive imaging biomarkers; however, manual segmentation of relevant brain structures is impractical for large cohorts and routine clinical workflows. In this study, we present a fully automated, deep learning–based image processing pipeline designed to support the differential diagnosis of APD. A region-based U-net model was developed to segment 12 deep-brain structures implicated in APD. By dividing the MRI volumes into anatomically targeted regions around the brainstem, ventricular system, and striatum, this approach reduces GPU memory demands and training time while maintaining competitive segmentation accuracy. The segmentation outputs, including masks and volumetric features, are then incorporated together with the T1-weighted MRI into a hybrid classification framework that combines convolutional neural networks with machine learning (ML) models to explore subtype differentiation in APD. By integrating spatial image features with quantitative structural biomarkers, we demonstrate the potential of this end-to-end pipeline to serve as a computational framework that may contribute to improved differential classification of APD.

nodes.name: A Survey on U-Net with Variants and Their Applications in Two-Dimensional Medical Image Segmentations
nodes.venue: Journal of Imaging
nodes.abstract: Medical image segmentation plays a critical role in computer-assisted diagnosis, treatment planning, surgical navigation, and quantitative medical image analysis. Among deep learning-based segmentation architectures, U-Net has become one of the most influential frameworks because of its encoder–decoder structure and skip connections for integrating semantic and spatial information. This review focuses on U-Net and representative variants for two-dimensional medical image segmentation. We systematically analyze their architectural evolution, including attention-based designs, enhanced skip connections, deformable convolutions, and Transformer-based extensions and discuss their advantages, limitations, and application boundaries. Quantitative performance results are synthesized from published studies rather than reproduced through new benchmarking experiments; direct numerical comparisons are restricted to models evaluated within the same study or under clearly defined benchmark settings. We further relate architectural modifications to modality-specific challenges in MRI, CT, ultrasound, fundus imaging, dermoscopy, and microscopy. Finally, current challenges in computational efficiency, cross-domain generalization, data scarcity, interpretability, and clinical deployment are discussed, together with promising directions for future research.

nodes.name: A Hybrid Model for Minimizing Malware Threats in Cloud Computing Using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Federated Learning (FL)
nodes.venue: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory
nodes.abstract: The objective of this study is to develop a hybrid model for minimizing malware threats in cloud computing model using Generative Adversary Networks (GANs) and Federated Learning (FL), to improve detection accuracy and reduce false positives using the hybrid model. The project was motivated by the prevailing challenges such as Model complexity, Data privacy and security, Malware detection in cloud computing, Data quality issues and Evaluation challenges. The methodology adopted is the Cross Industry Standard Process for Data Mining (CRISP- DM) hybrid methodology which involves structured data analysis, like fraud detection, customer segmentation. The programming language used for the implementation is python programming language. Expected results demonstrate significant improvement in detection accuracy, restore security in cloud computing practice ensuring confidence, integrity and privacy.

nodes.name: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory
Spatial Distribution and Cluster Analysis of the Population Aged 65 and Over at Neighbourhood Level in Erzurum Province
nodes.venue: Journal of Literature and Humanities
nodes.abstract: The aim of this study is to examine the spatial distribution of the population aged 65 and over at the neighbourhood level in Erzurum Province and to determine whether this distribution exhibits statistically significant clustering. In this study, the proportion of the elderly population at the neighbourhood level was calculated using data from the Turkish Statistical Institute’s (TURKSTAT) Address-Based Population Registration System and analysed within a Geographic Information Systems (GIS) environment. To identify spatial patterns, Global Moran’s I, Local Moran’s I (LISA) and Getis–Ord Gi* spatial autocorrelation analyses were applied. The findings reveal that the proportions of the elderly population at the neighbourhood level in Erzurum Province do not follow a random distribution and exhibit positive spatial autocorrelation. Global Moran’s I result indicate that neighbourhoods with similar proportions of the elderly population tend to cluster spatially. The Local Moran’s I (LISA) analysis revealed that high–high clusters are concentrated particularly in rural neighbourhoods within the districts of İspir, Uzundere, Tortum and Olur, while low–low clusters are found in the districts of Yakutiye, Palandöken and Aziziye. The Getis–Ord Gi* hot and cold spot analysis has confirmed these spatial patterns based on density and identified statistically significant hot spots, particularly in the northern parts of the province. The spatial distribution of the elderly population in Erzurum is largely shaped by rural–urban differences and migration processes. It is observed that in rural neighbourhoods, the proportion of the elderly population has increased alongside the migration of the younger population, whereas in urban centers, a more balanced or younger age structure prevails. This study provides methodological and analytical contributions to research examining the distribution of the elderly population using spatial statistical methods at the neighbourhood level. The findings also highlight the need for spatially targeted planning strategies to improve access to health, care, and social services in areas with high concentrations of elderly populations.

nodes.name: Product evolution model (PEM): a functional semantic knowledge-driven framework for product technology landscape construction
nodes.venue: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology
nodes.abstract: Purpose The construction of a product technology landscape remains heavily reliant on patent-based methods despite its recognized value in supporting the systematic product planning and technology opportunity identification. These patented approaches, however, are typically constrained to document-level operations such as retrieval, clustering and keyword analysis, creating a critical gap in their capacity to support the generation of component-level solutions. To address this gap, this study aims to propose a product evolution model (PEM), a functional semantic knowledge-driven framework that integrates patent-derived component knowledge, function–object–property (FOP) representation, TRIZ-based evolution trend label mapping, multi-objective optimization and TOPSIS-based decision ranking. Design/methodology/approach First, patent claims are transformed into product-component and component-FOP knowledge using the structured information extraction. Moreover, functional community detection and topic modeling are then used to identify representative components, while evolution trend labels are mapped to candidate components and incorporated into a component-evolution trend association matrix. The PEM formulates product technology landscape construction as a three-objective optimization problem that maximizes implementation effect, maximizes functional coverage and minimizes component count. Findings Using a new energy vehicle case study, the feasibility of the framework has been further demonstrated: from 873 initial component candidates, 654 valid components are retained after the semantic filtering and domain inspection, and 22 representative components are identified through the Louvain community detection and latent Dirichlet allocation topic modeling. Under the TOPSIS preference setting of 0.5 for the implementation effect, 0.2 for functional coverage and 0.3 for component count, the PEM selects a 19-component technology landscape solution with an implementation effect of 17.4375, a functional coverage of 0.9528 and a TOPSIS score of 0.6288. Originality/value The case study demonstrates the feasibility of PEM for supporting component-level technology landscape construction by connecting patent-derived functional semantics with evolution-oriented optimization and preference-sensitive decision ranking.

nodes.name: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology
Mitigating lateral sensing blind spots: A dual-segment bronchoscopic robot with a bioinspired skin
nodes.venue: Science Advances
nodes.abstract: Lateral force blind spots frequently trigger airway injuries during robotic bronchoscopy. Traditional sensing approaches lack fine spatial resolution, and single-segment robots suffer poor posture adjustment flexibility, worsening unmonitored tissue contact. We integrate a snake-scale-inspired 64-channel gradient piezoelectric film with a dual-segment manipulator to resolve lateral blind spots for secure bronchial navigation. The conformally wrapped sensor delivers fast (<10 ms), precise force detection ( R 2 > 0.98, RMSE < 0.145 N, CV < 2%) and filters bending pseudo-forces. The dual-segment design enables coordinated proximal-distal motion to avoid overcontact in tortuous lumens. Phantom and ex vivo porcine lung tests confirm real-time force localization, 5.0 N safety alarms, and autonomous tuning to keep contact forces below 3.0 N. This synergistic robot-sensor design supplies a translatable safety control strategy for flexible surgical manipulators.

nodes.name: Applications of quantum remote sensing in aerospace information systems
nodes.venue: Quantum Communications and Quantum Imaging XXIV
nodes.abstract:
Quantum remote sensing is defined as a theoretical and methodological framework that characterizes the laws of motion of remote sensing phenomena at the quantum level. It is grounded in quantum mechanics, employs the Schrödinger equation and quantum states as its principal modes of representation, and takes as its object of study the dynamic, multispatiotemporal planetary–Earth system. The field encompasses a comprehensive technological system, including theory, information processing, experimentation, computation, imaging, spectroscopy, measurement, and application. Its central objective is to investigate how information can be expressed, transmitted, and ultimately perceived through quantum states across the entire sensing chain. Compared with classical approaches, quantum remote sensing enables the acquisition of weaker, more microscopic, deeper, and richer information.

Quantum remote sensing was first proposed internationally by Professor Bi Siwen in 2000. The research program identifies four principal challenges: how to characterize the laws of motion of remote sensing processes at the quantum scale; how to realize the expression, transmission, and perceptual reception of information via quantum states; how quantum spectral imaging can be achieved, with emphasis on the characteristics of quantum spectra and the governing laws of spectral imaging; and how to conduct experimental investigations of quantum light-field imaging, as well as to advance the practical implementation and industrialization of quantum remote sensing imaging technologies.

Over twenty-six years of investigation, this research has yielded more than ten original innovations and has led to the development of eight prototype systems for quantum detection and quantum imaging. The work also presents an overview of the research team, its scientific outputs, and associated recognitions and awards.

At the systems level, an integrated panoramic framework for aerospace information-based quantum remote sensing is proposed. This framework comprises three principal components: quantum detection and sensing systems for aerospace information (0.5–900m range); quantum lidar systems (1–50km range); and quantum remote sensing observation systems (80, 300, and 500–800km orbital regimes).

The implementation of a quantum remote sensing scientific experimental satellite is further proposed, including the planned development, launch, and operation of a globally pioneering quantum remote sensing satellite. From a technological perspective, such systems offer substantial advantages, with significant implications for both aerospace information applications and military utilization.

The research team has completed studies on spaceborne active quantum remote sensing imaging schemes. The application of quantum remote sensing satellites is expected to have profound and far-reaching significance, particularly in the context of the emerging aerospace information.

nodes.name: Quantum Communications and Quantum Imaging XXIV
TSAR-Net: Transfer-Enhanced Local-to-Global Representation Learning for Micro-Doppler Classification of Small Aerial Targets
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Radar remote sensing provides an effective means of analyzing target characteristics for low-altitude surveillance, and the rapid growth and misuse of drones highlight the need for efficient classification of small aerial targets such as drones and birds. Micro-motions, such as rotor rotation or wing flapping, induce characteristic frequency shifts in radar echoes known as micro-Doppler effects. These radar-derived features provide essential structural and kinematic information for deep-learning-based target classification. However, in practical applications, existing methods still suffer from inadequate micro-Doppler feature extraction capability and rarely account for small-sample scenarios, both of which limit their classification performance. To address these challenges, this article proposes a transfer learning and self-attention enhanced ResNet50 (TSAR-Net), which combines transferred hierarchical convolutional features with multi-head self-attention to jointly exploit local and global time–frequency characteristics. Furthermore, to alleviate the small-sample classification problem, we introduce a projection-based TSAR-Net (PTSAR-Net), which maps the 2048-dimensional pooled feature through a 512-dimensional layer to a compact 128-dimensional representation for limited-label classification. On the measured DIAT-μSAT dataset, TSAR-Net achieves 99.59% accuracy, compared with 96.71% for VGG19, an improvement of 2.88 percentage points. With five training samples per class, PTSAR-Net achieves 81.14% accuracy, compared with 70.72% for TSAR-Net, an improvement of 10.42 percentage points.

nodes.name: Networked radiation detection architecture for CISA critical infrastructure protection
nodes.abstract: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has assumed responsibility for the Global Nuclear Detection Architecture (GNDA) following the dissolution of the Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction (CWMD) Office. This transition places nuclear and radiological detection within a broader national framework for infrastructure protection, emergency communications, and intergovernmental coordination. This paper presents a system-level assessment of CISA’s evolving nuclear detection architecture, with particular emphasis on Preventive Radiological and Nuclear Detection (PRND) and Consequence Management (CM) sensor suites. Drawing from the Department of Homeland Security’s System Assessment and Validation for Emergency Responders (SAVER) program, we evaluate commercial, government, military, and niche off-the-shelf radiation detection technologies in terms of performance, cost effectiveness, deployability, and integration potential. We further propose a photonics-enabled, multimodal communication architecture for large urban environments, integrating radiation sensors with real-time contextual data streams over resilient satellite and mobile ad hoc networks. The resulting framework aligns GNDA principles with CISA’s infrastructure security and emergency communication missions, while supporting international commitments under the Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material (CPPNM).

nodes.name: Litho-Hydraulic Planetary Cascade
nodes.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
nodes.abstract: Litho-Hydraulic Planetary Cascade (LHPC): A Unified Framework Integrating Crustal Pressure-Release Kernels, Sealed and Venting Zone Dynamics, Global Outgassing Telemetry, and Andean Sealed Segment Evolution This work presents the Litho-Hydraulic Planetary Cascade (LHPC) framework, a unified geophysical model that reconceptualizes Earth's lithosphere as a planetary-scale pressure-routing system governing the accumulation, migration, and episodic release of internally generated fluids and volatiles. The framework is intended as an extension to classical plate tectonic theory, introducing a mechanism to explain threshold-driven seismic cascades, variable outgassing behavior, and the spatial organization of pressure accumulation within active tectonic environments. 1 The LHPC framework is built around four interconnected components: Pressure-Release Kernels (PR-Kernels), defined as lithospheric pressure-accumulation units characterized by pressure ceiling, volatile inventory, seal integrity, and thermal state. Sealed and Venting Crust Regimes, a binary classification system describing whether crustal domains preferentially accumulate pressure or continuously dissipate fluids. Global Outgassing Telemetry (GOT), an integrated monitoring architecture combining satellite observations, hydrothermal datasets, geochemical measurements, seismic attenuation models, and geodetic networks to classify crustal behavior at regional to planetary scales. Andean Sealed Segment Evolution, a case study applying PR-Kernel analysis to the Nazca-South American subduction margin, reproducing observed segmentation patterns and interpreting major earthquake sequences, including the 2010 Maule and 2014 Iquique events, as cascade releases within a pressure-routing network. 1 The study proposes that a significant fraction of active subduction-margin crust exists in sealed or partially sealed states and that tectonic systems can be understood through the interaction of pressure accumulation, structural sealing, volatile transport, and threshold-triggered release. The framework further identifies the East Antarctic extensional province as a planetary-scale venting analog, providing a contrasting end-member to highly sealed convergent-margin environments. 1 Beyond terrestrial tectonics, LHPC extends to comparative planetology by examining how pressure-routing dynamics may operate on Venus, Mars, and Earth, offering a conceptual structure for evaluating planetary volatile cycling, lithospheric evolution, and long-term habitability. The framework also introduces testable predictions involving geodetic deformation, geochemical precursor signals, and cascade propagation behavior, establishing a foundation for future observational and modeling efforts. 1 Keywords: litho-hydraulic cascade, crustal fluid dynamics, pressure-release kernel, tectonics, earthquake cascades, volatile cycling, outgassing telemetry, subduction zones, Andes, Antarctica, geophysics, planetary geology, hazard assessment, comparative planetology.

How Much Do Earth-Observation Foundation Models Help Flood Mapping When Labels Are Scarce? Frozen, LoRA and Full Fine-Tuning of Prithvi-EO 2.0 on Sen1Floods11
nodes.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
nodes.abstract: Earth-observation foundation models are expected to reduce the number of labels needed for tasks such as flood mapping. We test this expectation in a controlled setting on the Sen1Floods11 benchmark. Two U-Nets (trained from scratch and ImageNet-initialized) are compared with Prithvi-EO 2.0, a 300M-parameter masked-autoencoder foundation model, under three fine-tuning regimes: frozen encoder, low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and full fine-tuning. All models see the same six Sentinel-2 bands and the same budget of optimizer steps, with 1% to 100% of the training labels (3 to 252 chips), three seeds per setting and 84 runs in total. The U-Nets lead at every label fraction: 0.829 versus 0.767 water IoU for Prithvi with LoRA at full labels, and 0.809 versus 0.704 with only three labeled chips. The gap therefore does not close as labels become scarce; it widens. Among the fine-tuning regimes, LoRA matches full fine-tuning (0.767 versus 0.770) with about 140 times fewer trainable parameters, and a frozen encoder trails both by about seven points. Pretraining also does not reduce the accuracy drop on the held-out Bolivia region. A pixel-level error analysis locates the foundation model's shortfall at water edges and on water bodies smaller than 0.1 km^2, consistent with its 16-pixel patch resolution. For Sentinel-2 flood mapping on this benchmark, a small well-tuned CNN remains the better choice, even with a handful of labeled scenes.

nodes.name: EarthCARE reveals details on the role of rain in closed-to-open cell transitions
nodes.venue: Atmospheric chemistry and physics
nodes.abstract: Abstract. The mesoscale organisation of marine stratocumulus clouds into closed and open cells strongly affects cloud albedo and thus their cooling effect on climate, yet the processes governing transitions between these regimes remain incompletely understood. The EarthCARE satellite provides collocated observations of cloud mesoscale structure from the Multi-Spectral Imager (MSI) together with vertically resolved cloud and precipitation measurements from the Atmospheric Lidar (ATLID) and Cloud Profiling Radar (CPR), enabling detailed characterization of stratocumulus cloud microphysics. We apply a convolutional neural network to MSI scenes to identify closed and open cells and relate these classifications to EarthCARE microphysical retrievals from the synergy of ATLID, CPR, and MSI. Open cells exhibit substantially lower droplet number concentrations (Nd), greater variability in liquid water path (LWP) and droplet sizes (re), and more frequent and heavier precipitation, although light drizzle is also common in closed cells. To investigate closed-to-open cell transitions, we combine EarthCARE overpasses with GOES/ABI geostationary imagery and ERA5-driven trajectories to track cloud scenes and determine transition timing. This combined approach allows us to reconstruct the temporal evolution of cloud properties around transitions. We find that LWP and rain amounts increase in closed cells up to ~25 hours before transitions, followed by decreasing Nd and increasing re, while cloud vertical structure remains largely unchanged. These findings support a precipitation-linked transition pathway, potentially triggered by enhanced boundary-layer moisture and amplified by aerosol scavenging–rain feedback. This new observational evidence advances our understanding of stratocumulus breakup with implications for the cooling effect of these clouds.

nodes.name: Deterministic correction of bitstream corruption in spaceborne JPEG images from the UVSQ-SatNG mission
nodes.abstract: Remote sensing missions rely on onboard image compression to optimize data transmission under strict bandwidth constraints. However, bitstream corruption can introduce chromatic distortions and block misalignments, significantly degrading the scientific usability of acquired images. Within the framework of the Uvsq-SatNG mission, launched in March 2025 for climate and atmospheric monitoring, tens of thousands of images have been acquired since April 2025 using a 3-megapixel RGB camera (MT9T031). These visible images are used for scene contextualization, cloud discrimination, surface characterization, and the validation of atmospheric retrieval products. Approximately 15% of the acquired images exhibit noticeable degradation caused by onboard compression and residual transmission errors, motivating the development of robust post-processing correction techniques. This work presents a non-neural, mathematically driven approach for restoring corrupted JPEG images acquired by the onboard Uvsq-SatNG RGB camera. The proposed method integrates a robust decoding strategy, a chromatic correction filter based on the Von Kries adaptation model, and a block realignment algorithm that models images as five-dimensional arrays of pixel blocks. This representation enables efficient detection and correction of spatial misalignments. Unlike deep learning–based restoration techniques, the proposed approach is fully deterministic, computationally lightweight, and does not require training data, making it suitable for both ground-based and onboard implementation. Experimental results obtained from in-orbit RGB images indicate substantial improvements in visual quality and radiometric consistency, thereby enhancing the reliability of downstream scientific analyses, including atmospheric correction and greenhouse gas retrieval. Beyond post-processing on the ground, the proposed method is compatible with future onboard processing architectures integrating FPGA- and RISC-V–based systems for real-time data handling, compression, and artificial intelligence. It can be used to automatically assess image quality, correct corrupted acquisitions, and selectively re-compress and transmit scientifically valuable scenes. This study highlights the relevance of physics-based and deterministic image restoration methods for operational CubeSat missions, onboard intelligent processing, and long-term Earth observation programs.

nodes.name: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND GEOSPATIAL TECHNOLOGIES FOR WATER QUALITY MONITORING: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF TRENDS, METHODS, AND RESEARCH GAPS INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL Y TECNOLOGÍAS GEOESPACIALES PARA EL MONITOREO DE LA CALIDAD DEL AGUA: UN ANÁLISIS BIBLIOMÉTRICO DE TENDENCIAS, MÉTODOS Y BRECHAS DE INVESTIGACIÓN INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL E TECNOLOGIAS GEOESPACIAIS PARA O MONITORAMENTO DA QUALIDADE DA ÁGUA: UMA ANÁLISE BIBLIOMÉTRICA DE TENDÊNCIAS, MÉTODOS E LACUNAS DE PESQUISA
nodes.venue: Revista de Geopolítica
nodes.abstract: Water quality monitoring is essential for ensuring the sustainable use of aquatic resources and preserving ecosystem health. The increasing application of artificial intelligence (AI) in this field has provided innovative approaches to modeling and predicting key water quality parameters with greater efficiency. This study aimed to map the landscape of scientific production, understand the correlation network among identified themes, and analyze the temporal evolution of publication output. We conducted a bibliometric analysis of scientific publications related to the use of AI in water quality assessment, employing tools such as Bibliometrix and VOSviewer. A total of 130 peer-reviewed articles were retrieved from the Web of Science and Scopus databases, covering the period from 2005 to 2025, and analyzed to identify research trends, key themes, and collaboration networks. Thematic clustering of keywords revealed four main research areas: (i) remote sensing, (ii) machine learning, (iii) water quality indicators, and (iv) hydrodynamic and watershed modeling. The results show that the term “machine learning” is central to the analyzed literature, connecting clusters focused on hydrological modeling, remote sensing, supervised learning algorithms, and the prediction of physicochemical variables. The findings highlight the interdisciplinary nature of the field and underscore the growing role of AI and geotechnologies as cost-effective tools for supporting water quality management, particularly in hard-to-access areas. These insights offer guidance for future research and help environmental agencies develop more efficient strategies for monitoring and preserving water resources.

nodes.name: Uncertainty quantification of hyperspectral scene reconstruction methods for high consequence remote sensing applications
nodes.venue: Applications of Machine Learning 2026
nodes.abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is a key capability for detecting chemical signatures of gases, liquids, or solids in remote sensing applications. Detection becomes challenging when targets are partially or fully occluded by objects in the scene. Three-dimensional scene understanding methods, including Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) and Gaussian Splatting (GS), provide a mechanism to cohesively synthesize multi-observation HSI data into a single scene representation, enabling the ability to effectively “look around” targets or obstructions. These approaches have shown promise for gas plume detection and identification; however, their limitations remain underexplored. We present an ensemble-based approach to quantify both spatial and spectral uncertainty. The proposed method achieves adequate uncertainty coverage and is model agnostic, making it applicable across a wide range of scene representation techniques. Importantly, we demonstrate cases where classic pixel-level metrics fail to indicate missing plume structure, giving a false sense of agreement. Our uncertainty quantification approach provides an efficient diagnostic cue that the model representation in these regions may be deficient, despite apparently reasonable performance metrics. For remote sensing applications, decision-makers require detection outputs accompanied by measures of confidence, particularly in complex environments where occlusions, atmospheric effects, or sparse measurements can degrade performance. By characterizing uncertainty, our method enables unreliable predictions to be flagged, supports prioritization of additional observations, and ultimately improves trust and robustness in HSI-based detection systems.

nodes.name: Toward likelihood-based latent video prediction for visual observation in drop-on-demand inkjet printing
nodes.venue: Photonic Fiber and Crystal Devices: Advances in Materials and Innovations in Device Applications XX
nodes.abstract: Predictive visual observation offers a pathway toward improved monitoring and eventual feedback control of drop-on-demand inkjet printing, where stroboscopic imaging provides repeated visual observations of the jetting process. We develop a two-stage latent video-prediction framework in which Stage 1 learns spatial latent representations using deterministic autoencoding, continuous variational autoencoding, or vector quantization, and Stage 2 performs likelihood-based temporal prediction using coordinate-conditioned Transformer context encoding, target-specific cross-attention, and a stochastic global context latent. The framework is evaluated on Moving-MNIST using a 2 × 2 × 4 factorial rubric spanning frame versus signed frame-difference domains, queryable versus autoregressive inference, and four latent representation/interface configurations. Stage-1 oracle analysis separates reconstruction limitations from temporal-prediction limitations. Frame-domain deterministic AE and continuous VAE predictions closely approach their Stage-1 reconstruction ceilings, whereas the frame-domain VQ foundation reconstructs accurately but exhibits severe Stage-2 code-prediction error. In the delta domain, autoregressive prediction outperforms queryable prediction across all four latent interfaces by deployable-frame MSE and SSIM, and a VAE mean-only interface outperforms direct inclusion of posterior log-variance by the same deployable-frame metrics. These results provide an initial controlled comparison of latent and temporal-prediction strategies under the present benchmark. A held-out Dimatix rollout provides an initial application-domain qualitative evaluation using historical continuous-VAE and VQ foundations, while broader aggregate application-domain validation remains future work. The present work evaluates prediction rather than closed-loop control or real-time execution.

Therapeutic Modulation of Glucocorticoid-Induced Sarcopenia by Boron: A Multimodal Preclinical Assessment
nodes.abstract: Abstract Boron is a bioactive trace element with emerging roles in musculoskeletal homeostasis and reported antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and cytoprotective properties. These biological activities make boron a potential candidate for targeting the multifactorial processes underlying skeletal muscle deterioration. Sarcopenia, characterized by progressive loss of muscle mass and function, remains a major therapeutic challenge, with no pharmacological treatment currently established specifically for restoring sarcopenia-related muscle loss and functional impairment. This unmet therapeutic need is particularly relevant to glucocorticoid-induced muscle wasting, a clinically important adverse consequence of prolonged glucocorticoid exposure. Despite its biological properties, the therapeutic potential of boron in glucocorticoid-induced sarcopenia remains largely unexplored. Therefore, this study investigated whether boron supplementation could promote functional and structural muscle recovery in a dexamethasone (DEX)-induced sarcopenia model in female Sprague–Dawley rats for the first time. After administering DEX (1 mg/kg/day, intraperitoneally) for 14 days, boron was given via drinking water at concentrations of 50 or 100 mg/L for 28 days. Muscle function was assessed through forelimb grip strength and hanging grid tests. The preservation of skeletal muscle was further evaluated with MRI, histopathological analysis, and muscle weight measurements. We also analyzed organ weights, serum biochemical parameters, and blood indices to assess systemic safety. Boron supplementation promoted functional and structural recovery following DEX-induced skeletal muscle wasting. By Day 42, forelimb grip strength was approximately 84–94% higher in boron-treated animals than in the untreated sarcopenia model (~ 6.5–6.8 vs. ~3.5 kgf), accompanied by greater preservation of skeletal muscle volume on MRI. Consistent with these functional and imaging findings, histopathological assessment demonstrated a dose-dependent attenuation of muscle atrophy, with atrophy scores reduced by approximately 50% and 80% following treatment with 50 and 100 mg/L boron, respectively ( p = 0.014 and p < 0.001 vs. the sarcopenia model). Importantly, boron treatment was not associated with overt adverse changes in major organ weights or the evaluated biochemical and hematological parameters, indicating favorable systemic tolerability under the experimental conditions. Collectively, these findings provide preclinical evidence that boron supplementation may promote functional and structural recovery following DEX-induced skeletal muscle wasting and support further mechanistic and translational investigation.

nodes.name: Technical Feasibility of a Multimodal Electro-Optical and Infrared Imaging Pipeline for Postoperative Wound Assessment After Total Knee Arthroplasty: Formative Evaluation Study
nodes.venue: JMIR Formative Research
nodes.abstract: Background Early detection and monitoring of wound-related complications after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) are critical to optimize outcomes and preserve implants. Conventional postoperative monitoring relies on in-person assessment and patient-reported symptoms, which may delay recognition. Noncontact imaging acquired in the clinic or at home offers a potential route to earlier and more consistent assessment. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the technical feasibility and performance of a multimodal AI system integrating electro-optical (EO) and infrared imaging for postoperative wound assessment following TKA and to explore clinical factors associated with early complications. Methods We conducted a single-center prospective cohort study of 749 patients undergoing primary TKA. Patients underwent standardized multimodal data collection at scheduled postoperative visits. EO-based models localized surgical landmarks and segmented complication-oriented tissue states; a fine-tuned vision-language model provided protocol verification and contextual visual reasoning. EO landmarks mapped to thermal space via deterministic alignment, followed by infrared region-of-interest segmentation and thermal classification. Each module was evaluated on a defined held-out set. The thermal classifier was assessed out-of-fold under 5-fold cross-validation with folds grouped by patient, in knees imaged on postoperative day 14 or later. Discrimination for clinician-adjudicated infection-related complications served as the primary outcome. Comorbidities and baseline laboratory values were explored for associations with complications. Results Among 749 patients, 26 (3.5%) had a clinician-adjudicated infection-related complication. On held-out evaluation, the EO landmark detector reached a sensitivity of 0.967 (95% CI 0.954-0.979) and positive predictive value of 0.955 (95% CI 0.940-0.970), and the wound-tissue segmentation model reached a sensitivity of 0.845 (95% CI 0.833-0.857) and positive predictive value of 0.759 (95% CI 0.744-0.772). Infrared region-of-interest extraction isolated the surgical field with a mean intersection-over-union of 0.985 (SD 0.008; 95% CI 0.984-0.986) across 178 held-out patients. The trained thermal classifier discriminated infected scans with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.978 (95% CI 0.959-0.992) in out-of-fold, patient-grouped cross-validation. At a representative operating point, sensitivity was 0.808 (95% CI 0.65-0.92), specificity 0.974 (95% CI 0.96-0.99), positive predictive value 0.618 (95% CI 0.49-0.78), and negative predictive value 0.990 (95% CI 0.98-1.00). Exploratory analyses showed nominal associations of chronic kidney disease and diabetes mellitus with postoperative complications that did not remain significant after multiplicity correction. Conclusions In this formative study, a multimodal EO and infrared imaging pipeline demonstrated technical feasibility for postoperative wound assessment following TKA, providing noncontact discrimination of infection-related complications that compared favorably with established adjuncts. This work provides proof-of-concept for multimodal imaging-based assessment and defines the technical requirements for the prospective, multicenter external validation needed to establish clinical utility.

nodes.name: Scenario-Based Assessment of Earth-Dam Stability Using Open Geospatial Data and Machine Learning: A Case Study of the Sherubay-Nur Reservoir, Kazakhstan
nodes.venue: Infrastructures
nodes.abstract: This article presents an integrated computational framework for scenario-based stability assessment of earth dams using open-access satellite data (Sentinel-2, Landsat 8/9), aerial imagery captured by UAVs, the FABDEM digital elevation model, and machine learning methods. The approach enables water surface detection, reservoir area calculation, water level reconstruction, and subsequent stability assessment via limit equilibrium modelling (Rocscience Slide2D). Tested on the Sherubay-Nur Reservoir (Kazakhstan), the method established a morphometric relationship between water level (534.20–536.80 m) and surface area (30.41–34.39 km2). Stability calculations showed a decrease in the factor of safety from 1.207 to 1.187 as the water level rose. Although all calculated values exceeded 1.0, this condition alone does not demonstrate compliance with the applicable stability criteria; the results indicate a consistent decrease in the factor of safety with increasing reservoir water level. The methodology developed does not replace field hydrometric, geodetic and geotechnical observations, but can be used as an additional analytical tool for retrospective analysis, supplementary model-based estimation of water levels and preliminary scenario-based assessment of the condition of hydraulic structures, particularly where on-site observations are incomplete or access to the site is restricted.
